title: The Keras Sequential API 🧱
description: Learn to stack layers one after another using the Sequential model.

slides.title: Two Ways to Build Models 🛠️
slides.content:
# 1. Sequential API
Layers are stacked in a straight line. Ideal for most simple networks.

# 2. Functional API
Layers can connect in complex graphs. More flexible, for multi‑input/output models.

We start with Sequential – it's like building a tower of blocks.

slides.title: Creating a Sequential Model
slides.codeSnippet:
# Way 1: list in constructor
model = Sequential([
    Dense(32, activation='relu'),
    Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

# Way 2: add() method
model = Sequential()
model.add(Dense(32, activation='relu'))
model.add(Dense(10, activation='softmax'))

# Way 3: with input_shape in first layer
model = Sequential()
model.add(Dense(32, activation='relu', input_shape=(784,)))
model.add(Dense(10, activation='softmax'))

quizData.question: Which statement about the Sequential API is TRUE?

options.text: Each layer's output feeds into the next layer
You can only use one hidden layer

quizData.explanation: Sequential models are linear stacks, each layer connected to the next.

slides.title: The `input_shape` Argument 📥
slides.content:
# Telling the Model What to Expect

You **must** specify the shape of the input data in the first layer (or via `model.build((batch, features))`).

- For a 28×28 image flattened, `input_shape=(784,)`.
- For a vector of 10 features, `input_shape=(10,)`.

**The batch dimension is omitted** – it's automatically handled.

slides.title: Checking Model Summary
slides.content: Use `model.summary()` to see the layer structure.
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Dense

model = Sequential([
    Dense(64, activation='relu', input_shape=(100,)),
    Dense(32, activation='relu'),
    Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
model.summary()

slides.title: No Weights Without `build` 🚧
slides.content: If you don't pass `input_shape`, the model is just a container. It will infer the shape and create weights only after the first batch of data or after calling `model.build(input_shape)`.
